g.say: Aquí es el mercado, ¿eh? ¿Se baja o sigue?
g.en: This is the market, OK? Are you getting off or staying on?

opts.why: Sigue means keep riding, and this is your stop.
Aquí es el mercado means you have arrived.

g.ph: ah-KEE ehs el mehr-KAH-doh, eh? seh BAH-hah oh SEE-geh?

end.en: There you go. That's thirty.
end.debrief: Colectivos shout their destination, so check with ¿Va a...? before you get in. You can often just say aquí me bajo to get off.

scenes.title: Late-night al pastor
scenes.blurb: Order at the trompo, handle ¿con todo?, and pay after.

a.say: ¿Qué le damos?
a.en: What can we get you?
a.task: You want three al pastor tacos.

opts.why: At a taco stand you order first and pay after. He is asking what you want.
¿Qué le damos? means what can we give you, and nada would send you away hungry.

opts.en: Can I have three al pastor?

a.ph: keh leh DAH-mohs?

opts.en: Whether you want all the toppings
Whether you want all the tacos at once
opts.why: Con todo means with everything on it. It has nothing to do with timing.
That would be ¿Es todo? or ¿Algo más? Con todo is about what goes on the taco.

c.en: It comes with cilantro, onion and a little pineapple, OK?

opts.why: Con mucha means with lots of it. To leave it out, say sin.
Sin todo means no toppings at all, so you would lose the cilantro and pineapple too.

c.ph: YEH-bah see-LAN-troh, seh-BOH-yah ee pee-NYEE-tah, bah?

d1.say: ¿Salsa roja o verde? La roja pica.
d1.en: Red or green salsa? The red one is hot.

opts.why: La roja pica means the red one is the hot one.
This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell him which salsa.

d1.ph: SAL-sah ROH-hah oh BEHR-deh? lah ROH-hah PEE-kah.

d2.say: Ya no hay piña, ¿eh? Se acabó. ¿Así está bien?
d2.en: There's no pineapple left, OK? It's finished. Is it fine like that?

opts.why: Ya no hay piña means there is none left to give you.
Se acabó means it ran out, so he isn't offering more.

d2.ph: yah noh eye PEE-nyah, eh? seh ah-kah-BOH. ah-SEE ehs-TAH byen?

e.en: All set? How many did you have?
e.task: A few minutes later. You ate three tacos.

opts.why: Cuántos means how many, not what time.
Cuántos fueron asks how many tacos you ate. He works out the price.

f.task: How much do you hand over?

opts.why: Cincuenta is 50. Sixty would be sesenta.
Cincuenta y cuatro is 54. Forty-five would be cuarenta y cinco.

end.en: Thanks. Take care.
end.debrief: At many taco stands you eat first and then say how many you had. Al pastor con todo usually means cilantro, onion and pineapple.

scenes.title: Night taxi up the hill
scenes.blurb: Agree the price first, find out how far he goes, say where to stop.

a.say: ¿Para dónde va?
a.en: Where are you headed?
a.task: You're going up the hill. Say so and ask the price.

opts.en: Here is fine, thank you very much.
opts.why: That is how you ask to get out, and you haven't got in yet.

opts.en: I'm doing very well, and you?
opts.why: ¿Para dónde va? means where are you going, not how are you.

opts.en: Up the hill. How much is it?

a.ph: PAH-rah DON-deh bah?

b1.en: All the way up? It's 80, at night.

opts.why: De noche just explains the price. He is offering to take you.
Ochenta is 80. Eighteen would be dieciocho.

b1.ph: AHS-tah ah-RREE-bah? son oh-CHEN-tah, deh NOH-cheh.

opts.why: He said ochenta, 80. Ochocientos is ten times that.
Ochenta is the price. Las ocho would be a time.

b2.say: Hasta arriba no subo, está feo el camino. Nomás hasta la entrada, son cincuenta.
b2.en: I don't go all the way up, the road is bad. Just to the entrance, it's 50.

opts.why: Hasta arriba no subo means he won't go all the way up.

opts.en: To wait for you at the top
opts.why: Nomás hasta la entrada means he stops at the entrance.

b2.ph: AHS-tah ah-RREE-bah noh SOO-boh, ehs-TAH FEH-oh el kah-MEE-noh. noh-MAHS AHS-tah lah en-TRAH-dah, son seen-KWEN-tah.

c2.en: Does that work, or will you look for another one?

opts.en: Yes, as far as the entrance.
Yes, I'm looking for the entrance.
opts.why: Busca otro asks if you would rather find another taxi.
He just said he won't drive up there.

d.say: Ya casi llegamos. ¿Aquí o más adelante?
d.en: We're nearly there. Here or further on?
d.task: A few minutes later. You want to stop here.

opts.why: Más adelante would take you past where you want to get out.
He is asking where to stop, not how fast to go.

d.ph: yah KAH-see yeh-GAH-mohs. ah-KEE oh mahs ah-deh-LAN-teh?

e.say: Ya llegamos. Lo que quedamos, ¿eh? ¿Trae cambio?
e.en: Here we are. What we agreed, OK? Do you have change?

opts.why: Lo que quedamos means the price you already agreed on.
Cambio here is small change, so he isn't asking about exchanging money.

e.ph: yah yeh-GAH-mohs. loh keh keh-DAH-mohs, eh? TRAH-eh KAM-byoh?

end.en: Thanks, rest well.
end.debrief: Agree the price before you get in. Some drivers won't take a steep, bad road at night, and aquí está bien is all you need to stop.

scenes.title: Red flag
scenes.blurb: Understand a shouted warning and get out of the water.

a.say: ¡Oiga! ¡Salga del agua! ¡Bandera roja!
a.en: Hey! Get out of the water! Red flag!
a.task: What is he telling you?

opts.en: Swim further out, the water is better there
opts.why: Salga means get out, so he is calling you in.

opts.en: Get out of the water now
Go and stand by the red flag
opts.why: Bandera roja means swimming is too dangerous. It's a warning, not a meeting place.

a.ph: OY-gah! SAL-gah del AH-gwah! ban-DEH-rah ROH-hah!

b1.say: Hay mucha corriente. Aquí jala para adentro.
b1.en: There's a strong current. Right here it pulls you out to sea.
b1.task: You're out of the water. Ask where you can swim.

opts.why: Para adentro means out toward the open sea, which is exactly what he is warning you about.

opts.en: Should I run to the shore?
opts.why: Corriente is the current in the water. He isn't telling you to run.

b1.ph: eye MOO-chah koh-RRYEN-teh. ah-KEE HAH-lah PAH-rah ah-DEN-troh.

b2.say: Ya entraron las olas grandes. Hoy no se mete nadie.
b2.en: The big waves have come in. Nobody goes in today.

opts.en: Just for a little while, no?
opts.why: No se mete nadie means nobody at all goes in.
He is telling you the waves are the danger. This isn't good surf news.

b2.ph: yah en-TRAH-ron lahs OH-lahs GRAN-dehs. oy noh seh MEH-teh NAH-dyeh.

c1.say: Aquí no se puede. Hoy mejor nomás mójese los pies.
c1.en: You can't here. Today, better just get your feet wet.

opts.why: Hoy mejor nomás means that is all you should do today.
Aquí no se puede means no swimming here. He only allowed your feet.

c1.ph: ah-KEE noh seh PWEH-deh. oy meh-HOR noh-MAHS MOH-heh-seh lohs pyehs.

c2.say: Mañana, a ver. Depende de la bandera.
c2.en: Tomorrow, we'll see. It depends on the flag.
c2.task: How will you know about tomorrow?

opts.en: Check the color of the flag

opts.why: Depende de la bandera means the flag decides.

opts.en: It will definitely be fine tomorrow
opts.why: A ver means we'll see, so it is not a promise.

c2.ph: mah-NYAH-nah, ah behr. deh-PEN-deh deh lah ban-DEH-rah.

d.say: Y cuando hay corriente, no nade en contra. Nade de lado, paralelo a la playa.
d.en: And when there's a current, don't swim against it. Swim sideways, parallel to the beach.

opts.why: De lado means sideways, parallel to the beach, in either direction.
No nade en contra means do not swim against it.

d.ph: ee KWAN-doh eye koh-RRYEN-teh, noh NAH-deh en KON-trah. NAH-deh deh LAH-doh, pah-rah-LEH-loh ah lah PLAH-yah.

end.en: That's it. Take care.
end.debrief: Zipolite's surf and rip currents are dangerous. Obey the flags and the lifeguards, and if a current takes you, swim sideways along the shore.

scenes.title: Stomach trouble
scenes.blurb: Explain the problem and find out how to take what she gives you.

a.say: Buenas tardes, ¿en qué le ayudo?
a.en: Good afternoon, how can I help you?
a.task: Your stomach hurts.

opts.why: She isn't asking how you are. En qué le ayudo means how can I help.
She has offered to help, so now she needs to know what's wrong.

a.ph: BWEH-nahs TAR-dehs, en keh leh ah-YOO-doh?

b.en: Do you have diarrhea or vomiting? Since when?

opts.why: This isn't an offer. She needs to know which symptom and since when.
Desde cuándo means since when, so you need a time in the past. Ayer is yesterday.

b.ph: TYEH-neh dyah-RREH-ah oh BOH-mee-toh? DEHS-deh KWAN-doh?

c1.say: Le puedo dar loperamida y suero. ¿Trae calentura?
c1.en: I can give you loperamide and rehydration drink. Do you have a fever?
c1.task: You have no fever. Ask how to take the medicine.

opts.why: Calentura means a fever. Tengo calor is about the weather.
Suero here is a rehydration drink, so nobody is giving you a shot.

opts.en: No. How do you take it?

c1.ph: leh PWEH-doh dar loh-peh-rah-MEE-dah ee SWEH-roh. TRAH-eh kah-len-TOO-rah?

c2.say: Le puedo dar loperamida y suero. ¿Tiene fiebre o ha visto sangre? Porque si sí, mejor vaya con el doctor.
c2.en: I can give you loperamide and rehydration drink. Do you have a fever or have you seen blood? Because if so, you should go to the doctor.
c2.task: No, it's only diarrhea. Ask how to take the medicine.

opts.es: Sin sangre, por favor. ¿Cómo se toma?
opts.en: No blood, please. How do you take it?
opts.why: Sangre is a symptom she is asking about. It isn't something she is offering.
opts.ph: seen SAN-greh, por fah-BOR. KOH-moh seh TOH-mah?

opts.en: Just diarrhea. How do you take it?
opts.ph: NAH-dah mahs dyah-RREH-ah. KOH-moh seh TOH-mah?

opts.es: Sí, voy al doctor. ¿Dónde hay uno?
opts.en: Yes, I'm going to the doctor. Where is one?
opts.why: She said to see a doctor only if you have fever or blood, and you don't.
opts.ph: see, boy al dohk-TOR. DON-deh eye OO-noh?

c2.ph: leh PWEH-doh dar loh-peh-rah-MEE-dah ee SWEH-roh. TYEH-neh FYEH-breh oh ah BEES-toh SAN-greh? POR-keh see see, meh-HOR BAH-yah kon el dohk-TOR.

d.say: Como dice la caja. Y mucho suero, ¿eh?
d.en: The way the box says. And plenty of rehydration drink, OK?
d.task: How should you take the medicine?

opts.why: Como dice la caja means the way the box says, not the whole box.
Como dice la caja means follow the directions on the box.

d.ph: KOH-moh DEE-seh lah KAH-hah. ee MOO-choh SWEH-roh, eh?

e.say: Y no coma picante ni lácteos. ¿Algo más?
e.en: And don't eat spicy food or dairy. Anything else?
e.task: That's all. Ask how much it is.

opts.en: That's all. How much is it?

opts.why: No coma picante means do not eat spicy food.
Lácteos means dairy, so she just told you to avoid milk.

e.ph: ee noh KOH-mah pee-KAN-teh nee LAHK-teh-ohs. AL-goh mahs?

end.say: Son doscientos diez. Que se mejore.
end.en: It's 210. Get well soon.
end.debrief: Pharmacists in Mexico will often suggest something if you describe the problem. Follow the directions on the box, and see a doctor for fever, blood, or if it doesn't get better.
end.ph: son dohs-SYEN-tohs dyehs. keh seh meh-HOH-reh.

scenes.title: The bill and a dead terminal
scenes.blurb: Ask for the bill, keep it together, and be ready to pay cash.

a.say: ¿Todo bien? ¿Se les ofrece algo más?
a.en: Everything OK? Can I get you anything else?
a.task: You're finished. Ask for the bill.

opts.why: La carta is the menu. The bill is la cuenta.
Algo más means anything else, so sí tells her you want more.

a.ph: TOH-doh byen? seh lehs oh-FREH-seh AL-goh mahs?

b.task: One person is paying for everything.

opts.why: Separada means one bill per person. One person is paying, so you want it junta.
This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell her which one.
Ochocientos cuarenta is 840. Eighty-four would be ochenta y cuatro.
Ochocientos is 800. Four hundred would be cuatrocientos.

d.en: How are you going to pay?

opts.why: She knows the amount. Cómo asks how you will pay.
Cómo means how, so this isn't a yes/no question.

e1.say: Ahorita le traigo la terminal. ¿Le agrego la propina?
e1.en: I'll bring the card machine right away. Shall I add the tip?

opts.why: Propina is the tip. She isn't offering you more to drink.
The machine is on its way and you chose card. This question is about the tip.

e1.ph: ah-oh-REE-tah leh TRY-goh lah tehr-mee-NAL. leh ah-GREH-goh lah proh-PEE-nah?

end1.debrief: Servers rarely bring the bill until you ask, and the card machine comes to your table. A tip of 10 to 15 percent is usual.

e2.say: Uy, fíjese que no está pasando la terminal, se cayó el sistema. ¿No trae efectivo?
e2.en: Oh, you know what, the card machine isn't going through, the system is down. Do you have cash on you?

opts.why: No está pasando la terminal means cards aren't working at all right now.
She isn't offering anything. She needs another way for you to pay.

e2.ph: wee, FEE-heh-seh keh noh ehs-TAH pah-SAN-doh lah tehr-mee-NAL, seh kah-YOH el sees-TEH-mah. noh TRAH-eh eh-fehk-TEE-boh?

f.say: Qué pena. ¿Trae cambio o nada más billete grande?
f.en: So sorry. Do you have change, or just a big bill?
f.task: You only have a thousand-peso note.

opts.why: Cambio is small change here, not currency exchange.
She knows the total. She wants to know what size of bill you are holding.

f.ph: keh PEH-nah. TRAH-eh KAM-byoh oh NAH-dah mahs bee-YEH-teh GRAN-deh?

end2.say: No se apure, ahorita le traigo su cambio.
end2.en: Don't worry, I'll bring your change right away.
end2.debrief: When the card machine goes down, you pay cash, so keep some on you. Small bills make everything easier.
end2.ph: noh seh ah-POO-reh, ah-oh-REE-tah leh TRY-goh soo KAM-byoh.

scenes.title: The dish is gone
scenes.blurb: Order mole, cope if they ran out, and pick a side.

a.say: Buenas tardes. ¿Ya sabe qué va a ordenar?
a.en: Good afternoon. Do you know what you'd like to order?
a.task: Order the chicken in black mole.

opts.en: Yes, I already ate, thanks very much.
opts.why: Ya sabe asks whether you know what you want yet. She isn't asking if you have eaten.

opts.en: Can you bring me the bill, please?
opts.why: She is asking for your order, and that asks for the bill.
opts.ph: meh TRAH-eh lah KWEN-tah, por fah-BOR?

opts.es: ¿Me da el pollo con mole negro?
opts.en: Can I have the chicken in black mole?
opts.ph: meh dah el POH-yoh kon MOH-leh NEH-groh?

a.ph: BWEH-nahs TAR-dehs. yah SAH-beh keh bah ah or-deh-NAR?

b1.en: Perfect. With rice or with beans?
b1.task: Pick one side. Either is fine.

opts.why: This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell her which one.

opts.en: No rice, thank you very much.
opts.why: Sin means without. She is offering a choice of side, so name the one you want.

b1.ph: pehr-FEHK-toh. kon ah-RROHS oh kon free-HOH-lehs?

b2.say: Ay, fíjese que ya se nos acabó el negro. Ahorita nada más tengo el coloradito.
b2.en: Oh, you know what, we ran out of the black one. Right now I only have the coloradito.
b2.task: What did she just tell you?

opts.en: The black mole is coming right now
opts.why: Ahorita goes with nada más tengo: right now she only has the other one.

opts.en: They're out, only coloradito is left
The black mole will take a little longer
opts.why: Se nos acabó means they ran out. It isn't a delay.

b2.ph: eye, FEE-heh-seh keh yah seh nohs ah-kah-BOH el NEH-groh. ah-oh-REE-tah NAH-dah mahs TEN-goh el koh-loh-rah-DEE-toh.

b3.en: Shall I bring it with coloradito, then?

opts.why: Sin means without. That would be chicken with no sauce at all.
She just told you the black mole is gone, so she can't bring it.

b3.ph: seh loh TRY-goh kon koh-loh-rah-DEE-toh, en-TON-sehs?

c.say: Órale. ¿Y de tomar qué le traigo?
c.en: OK. And what can I bring you to drink?
c.task: Ask for a lime agua fresca.

opts.ph: meh dah oon AH-gwah deh lee-MON?

opts.why: The side is settled. De tomar means something to drink.
Tomar here means to drink. Para llevar would turn your meal into takeout.

c.ph: OH-rah-leh. ee deh toh-MAR keh leh TRY-goh?

end.en: Perfect, I'll bring it right over.
end.debrief: Se nos acabó and ya no hay both mean they ran out. From a server, ahorita usually means soon, not this second.

scenes.title: Airport driver and the ATM
scenes.blurb: Meet your driver, stop for cash, and cope with an empty ATM.

a.say: ¿Reservación para Zipolite? Yo soy el chofer.
a.en: Reservation for Zipolite? I'm the driver.
a.task: That's you. Greet him.

opts.why: He is the driver. He is checking that you are the passenger.
He is confirming your booking, and no would send him away.

a.ph: reh-sehr-bah-SYON PAH-rah see-poh-LEE-teh? yoh soy el choh-FEHR.

b.say: Perfecto. ¿Nomás esa maleta? Vámonos, está largo el camino.
b.en: Great. Just that suitcase? Let's go, it's a long way.
b.task: You need cash. Ask to stop at an ATM.

opts.why: ¿Nomás esa maleta? means just that suitcase? You are keeping your bag.

opts.es: No, esa maleta está muy larga.
opts.en: No, that suitcase is very long.
opts.why: Largo means long, and he is talking about the road, not your suitcase.
opts.ph: noh, EH-sah mah-LEH-tah ehs-TAH mwee LAR-gah.

opts.en: Can we stop at an ATM?

b.ph: pehr-FEHK-toh. noh-MAHS EH-sah mah-LEH-tah? BAH-moh-nohs, ehs-TAH LAR-goh el kah-MEE-noh.

c.say: Hay uno en la gasolinera, pero luego no tiene dinero. ¿Probamos?
c.en: There's one at the gas station, but sometimes it has no money. Shall we try?

opts.why: Luego here means sometimes. He isn't suggesting you do it later.
He said the ATM may be out of money. You still need some.

c.ph: eye OO-noh en lah gah-soh-lee-NEH-rah, PEH-roh LWEH-goh noh TYEH-neh dee-NEH-roh. proh-BAH-mohs?

d1.say: ¿Ya? Qué bueno, ese sí tiene dinero. Vámonos.
d1.en: Done? Good, that one does have money. Let's go.
d1.task: You got your cash. You're ready.

opts.why: This one worked, so there's no need to find another.
Sí tiene dinero means it does have money.

d1.ph: yah? keh BWEH-noh, EH-seh see TYEH-neh dee-NEH-roh. BAH-moh-nohs.

d2.say: Ya ve, dice fuera de servicio, sin efectivo. ¿No trae nada?
d2.en: You see, it says out of service, no cash. You have nothing on you?

opts.en: Yes, that one does have service.
opts.why: Fuera de servicio means out of order.
He is asking how much cash you have, and you only have 400.

d2.ph: yah beh, DEE-seh FWEH-rah deh sehr-BEE-syoh, seen eh-fehk-TEE-boh. noh TRAH-eh NAH-dah?

f.say: No se apure. Allá en Pochutla hay más cajeros, nos queda de paso.
f.en: Don't worry. There are more ATMs in Pochutla, it's on our way.

opts.en: Skip paying him until you have cash
opts.why: He didn't say that. He is only telling you where more cajeros are.

opts.en: Try ATMs in Pochutla on the way
Go back to the airport to find one
opts.why: Nos queda de paso means it is on the way, so you keep going.

f.ph: noh seh ah-POO-reh. ah-YAH en poh-CHOO-tlah eye mahs kah-HEH-rohs, nohs KEH-dah deh PAH-soh.

e.say: Entonces, como quedamos: mil doscientos, cuando lleguemos.
e.en: So, as we agreed: 1,200, when we get there.
e.task: How much do you pay, and when?

opts.why: Cuando lleguemos means when you arrive.
Mil doscientos is 1,200, and cuando lleguemos means when you arrive.

e.ph: en-TON-sehs, KOH-moh keh-DAH-mohs: meel dohs-SYEN-tohs, KWAN-doh yeh-GEH-mohs.

end.say: Ándele, súbase. Atrás hay agua, por si gusta.
end.en: There you go, get in. There's water in the back if you'd like some.
end.debrief: ATMs on the coast are few and often empty, so get cash wherever one works. Fuera de servicio and sin efectivo are the signs to look for.
end.ph: AN-deh-leh, SOO-bah-seh. ah-TRAHS eye AH-gwah, por see GOOS-tah.

scenes.title: Bargaining for a rug
scenes.blurb: Ask the price, make one polite offer, and settle.

a.say: Pásele, sin compromiso. Todo es de lana, teñido a mano.
a.en: Come in, no obligation. Everything is wool, hand-dyed.
a.task: Ask how much this rug is.

opts.why: Sin compromiso is her saying you can look without having to buy.
Lana can be slang for money, but here it means wool.

a.ph: PAH-seh-leh, seen kom-proh-MEE-soh. TOH-doh ehs deh LAH-nah, teh-NYEE-doh ah MAH-noh.

b.ph: EH-seh seh loh DEH-hoh en dohs meel oh-choh-SYEN-tohs. ehs POO-roh TEEN-teh nah-too-RAL, YEH-bah KOH-moh dohs MEH-sehs deh trah-BAH-hoh.

opts.why: ¿Le gusta? is her asking you, so tell her.

opts.ph: meh loh DEH-hah en dohs meel?

d1.en: Oh no, 2,000 doesn't work for me. I'll let it go for 2,400, that's my lowest.

opts.en: Yes, but for two thousand, right?
opts.why: No me sale means she can't sell it at that price.
opts.ph: see, PEH-roh en dohs meel, noh?

d1.ph: eye, noh, dohs meel noh meh SAH-leh. seh loh DEH-hoh en dohs meel kwah-troh-SYEN-tohs, ehs loh MEH-nohs.

d2.en: Look, if you take two, I'll let them go for 4,500.

opts.es: Sí, cuatro mil quinientos por uno.

end.en: Thank you very much. Here is your rug, enjoy it.

end.ph: MOO-chahs GRAH-syahs. ah-KEE ehs-TAH soo tah-PEH-teh, keh loh dees-FROO-teh.

scenes.title: Buying a van seat
scenes.blurb: First van is full. Take the next one and sort out your bags.

opts.why: She isn't asking how you are. ¿A dónde viaja? means where are you traveling to.

a.ph: BWEH-nohs DEE-ahs. ah DON-deh BYAH-hah?

b1.en: The seven o'clock is already full. I have seats left on the nine thirty.

opts.why: Ya va llena means it is already full.
Y media is half past. A quarter past would be y cuarto.

b2.say: Sí hay, pero nada más dos lugares hasta atrás.

You are two people, and two seats are exactly what she has.

b2.ph: see eye, PEH-roh NAH-dah mahs dohs loo-GAH-rehs AHS-tah ah-TRAHS.

c.task: You have two suitcases between you.

opts.why: Los dos means the two of you, and the seats are settled. She is asking how you will pay.
This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell her how you will pay.

e.ph: son oh-choh-SYEN-tohs lohs dohs. eh-fehk-TEE-boh oh tar-HEH-tah?

end.say: Aquí están sus boletos. Lleguen quince minutos antes, no esperan.
end.en: Here are your tickets. Get here fifteen minutes early, they don't wait.

end.ph: ah-KEE ehs-TAN soos boh-LEH-tohs. YEH-gen KEEN-seh mee-NOO-tohs AN-tehs, noh ehs-PEH-ran.

scenes.title: Coffee to go

a.en: Hi, good morning. What can I make you?
a.task: You want a coffee with milk.

b1.en: With whole milk, lactose-free or almond?

She is only asking which milk, and you did order milk.

opts.why: She still has café de olla. Only the machine broke.

opts.why: Algo más means anything else, so sí means you do want something more.

d.ph: AL-goh mahs? teh-NEH-mohs KON-chahs reh-SYEN sah-LEE-dahs del OR-noh.

e.say: Son sesenta y cinco, por favor.

opts.why: Sesenta y cinco is 65. Fifty-six would be cincuenta y seis.

e.ph: son seh-SEN-tah ee SEEN-koh, por fah-BOR.

scenes.title: Finding your Uber
scenes.blurb: A phone call with a confused driver about which corner.

a.say: ¿Bueno? ¿Usted pidió el Uber? Ya llegué, pero no veo a nadie.
a.en: Hello? Did you order the Uber? I'm here, but I don't see anyone.
a.task: Yes, it's you. Ask where he is.

opts.why: ¿Bueno? is how people answer the phone in Mexico. It doesn't mean good.
He is asking if you ordered the ride, and no would make him cancel it.

b1.say: Aquí en la esquina, frente a la farmacia.
b1.en: Right here on the corner, across from the pharmacy.

opts.why: Frente a means across from. He is in the car on the corner.

opts.en: On the corner, facing the pharmacy
Two blocks away from the pharmacy
opts.why: En la esquina means right on the corner.

b1.ph: ah-KEE en lah ehs-KEE-nah, FREN-teh ah lah far-MAH-syah.

b2.say: Este... la aplicación me marca del otro lado del parque. ¿Usted dónde está?

b2.task: You're on the corner by the Oxxo.

opts.en: Yes, I'm on the other side.

The app is what is confusing him. He needs a real place he can see.

opts.ph: en lah ehs-KEE-nah, en el OHK-soh.

b2.ph: EHS-teh... lah ah-plee-kah-SYON meh MAR-kah del OH-troh LAH-doh del PAR-keh. oos-TEHD DON-deh ehs-TAH?

opts.en: A gray Aveo, plates ending in 47
A gray Aveo, plates ending in 74

scenes.title: Happy hour and last call
scenes.blurb: Use a 2x1, order another round, and catch closing time.

a.say: ¿Qué onda? Hay dos por uno en chelas hasta las ocho.
a.en: Hey, what's up? It's two-for-one on beers until eight.
a.task: What's the deal?

opts.why: Dos por uno means two for the price of one. It isn't a price.

opts.en: Two for the price of one, until 8
You have to order two beers at 8

Oscuras means dark beers. Claras are the light ones.
This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell him which.
Clara is the kind of beer on offer, and sin clara refuses the only one he has.
¿Va? here means is that OK. He isn't asking you to go anywhere.

c2.ph: yah NAH-dah mahs KEH-dah KLAH-rah, bah?

d.en: Another round? The two-for-one is over, you know.

It is already past eight. Ya se acabó means the deal is over.

d.ph: OH-trah RON-dah? yah seh ah-kah-BOH el dohs por OO-noh, eh?

scenes.title: Last shuttle, friend missing
scenes.blurb: Find the stop, catch the last bus time, and get help finding your friend.

a.say: Buenas noches, ¿busca el transporte de regreso?
a.en: Good evening, are you looking for the shuttle back?
a.task: Yes. Ask where the stop is.

opts.why: She is offering to help you leave, so no turns the help down.
Regreso here is the ride back tonight. She isn't asking when.

a.ph: BWEH-nahs NOH-chehs, BOOS-kah el trans-POR-teh deh reh-GREH-soh?

b1.task: When does the last bus leave?

opts.why: La una is one o'clock, and y media adds half an hour.
Y media is half past. A quarter past would be y cuarto.

opts.why: Ya salió refers to the one o'clock. The last one is still to come.

Will you wait for me here?

opts.why: El camión no espera means the bus won't wait.

end2.ph: keh BWEH-noh. KOH-rran-leh, keh yah seh YEH-nah.

How much is it for the chair?

scenes.title: No power at the house

Only your house has no power

opts.why: Reportaron means people reported the outage.

b1.ph: ah-oh-REE-tah ehs-TAH YEH-noh. eye KOH-moh kwah-REN-tah mee-NOO-tohs deh ehs-PEH-rah.

c.en: Shall I put you on the list?

opts.why: La lista here is the waitlist. The menu is la carta, and you have no table yet.
Cuarenta was minutes of waiting. Nobody is charging you to go on the list.

d.task: Give a name. Alex is only a practice name, so use your own in real life.

opts.why: De quién means of whom. He wants a name, and de nada answers a thank-you.

opts.en: There are two of us, please.
opts.why: He already knows how many. A nombre de quién asks for the name.

e.say: Listo. Yo les aviso cuando esté su mesa. ¿Gustan esperar en la barra?
e.en: All set. I'll let you know when your table is ready. Would you like to wait at the bar?

opts.why: Gustan esperar is an invitation to wait somewhere. There is nothing to pay yet.
Cuando esté su mesa means when it is ready, and it isn't yet.

e.ph: LEES-toh. yoh lehs ah-BEE-soh KWAN-doh ehs-TEH soo MEH-sah. GOOS-tan ehs-peh-RAR en lah BAH-rrah?

end.en: Sure, come this way.
end.debrief: Popular places in Condesa often have a wait for walk-ins. Give a short, easy name, because it will be called out across the room.

b2.say: Tienen suerte, se acaba de desocupar una. ¿Adentro o en la terraza?
b2.en: You're in luck, one just opened up. Inside or on the terrace?

opts.en: What time does it free up?
opts.why: Se acaba de desocupar means a table just freed up, so there is no wait.
This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell him where to seat you.

b2.ph: TYEH-nen SWER-teh, seh ah-KAH-bah deh deh-soh-koo-PAR OO-nah. ah-DEN-troh oh en lah teh-RRAH-sah?

b3.say: Pásenle. ¿Les traigo agua mientras ven la carta?
b3.en: Come on through. Shall I bring you water while you look at the menu?

opts.why: La carta is the menu. La cuenta is the bill, and you only just sat down.

opts.en: How long do we have to wait?
opts.why: You are already being seated. Mientras ven la carta means while you read the menu.

b3.ph: PAH-sen-leh. lehs TRY-goh AH-gwah MYEN-trahs ben lah KAR-tah?

end2.debrief: If a table happens to be free, you'll get a quick choice of where to sit: adentro or en la terraza.

scenes.title: Overweight at check-in
scenes.blurb: Your bag is over the limit. Move things or pay.

a.say: Buenas tardes. Su pase de abordar, por favor. ¿Cuántas maletas documenta?
a.en: Good afternoon. Your boarding pass, please. How many bags are you checking?
a.task: You're checking one.

opts.why: Cuántas maletas asks about suitcases.
Documentar here means to check a bag. She isn't asking for papers.

a.ph: BWEH-nahs TAR-dehs. soo PAH-seh deh ah-bor-DAR, por fah-BOR. KWAN-tahs mah-LEH-tahs doh-koo-MEN-tah?

b1.say: Trae veintitrés kilos y su tarifa incluye dieciocho. Son cinco de sobrepeso.
b1.en: It's 23 kilos and your fare includes 18. That's five overweight.
b1.task: How many kilos over are you?

opts.why: Veintitrés is the whole bag. Sobrepeso is only the part above your limit.
Cinco is 5. Fifteen would be quince.

b1.ph: TRAH-eh bayn-tee-TREHS KEE-lohs ee soo tah-REE-fah een-KLOO-yeh dyeh-SYOH-choh. son SEEN-koh deh soh-breh-PEH-soh.

c.say: Puede pagar el sobrepeso, o sacar cosas y pasarlas a su mochila.
c.en: You can pay for the excess, or take things out and put them in your backpack.

opts.why: This was an either/or choice, so sí doesn't tell her which you want.
Sobrepeso is what the scale shows. It isn't something you can decline.

opts.en: I'm going to take things out.

c.ph: PWEH-deh pah-GAR el soh-breh-PEH-soh, oh sah-KAR KOH-sahs ee pah-SAR-lahs ah soo moh-CHEE-lah.

d.say: A ver, súbala otra vez. Diecinueve. Todavía trae uno de más.
d.en: Let's see, put it up again. Nineteen. You're still one over.

opts.why: Todavía means still, so you are not done yet.
Diecinueve is the weight in kilos.

opts.en: How much is it for one kilo?

d.ph: ah behr, SOO-bah-lah OH-trah behs. dyeh-see-NWEH-beh. toh-dah-BEE-ah TRAH-eh OO-noh deh mahs.

e.say: Son trescientos cincuenta. Se paga en caja, aquí a un lado, y me trae el recibo.
e.en: It's 350. You pay at the cashier, right next to here, and bring me the receipt.

opts.en: Pay her here at the desk and wait for a receipt
opts.why: En caja, aquí a un lado means at the cashier next to her desk.

opts.en: Pay next door, then bring back the receipt
Wait here for her to give you 350 pesos
opts.why: Se paga means you pay it.

e.ph: son trehs-SYEN-tohs seen-KWEN-tah. seh PAH-gah en KAH-hah, ah-KEE ah oon LAH-doh, ee meh TRAH-eh el reh-SEE-boh.

end.say: Perfecto, con eso ya queda. Buen vuelo.
end.en: Perfect, that takes care of it. Have a good flight.
end.debrief: Low-cost airlines weigh bags strictly. The limits and fee in this scene are made up, so check your own booking for your real allowance.
end.ph: pehr-FEHK-toh, kon EH-soh yah KEH-dah. bwen BWEH-loh.

b2.say: La maleta va bien, pero la de mano también se pesa. Póngala aquí, por favor.
b2.en: The suitcase is fine, but the carry-on gets weighed too. Put it here, please.

opts.en: Put your carry-on on the scale

opts.why: Póngala aquí means put it here.

opts.en: Put your suitcase on the scale again
opts.why: La de mano is your carry-on, and the suitcase already passed.

b2.ph: lah mah-LEH-tah bah byen, PEH-roh lah deh MAH-noh tam-BYEN seh PEH-sah. PON-gah-lah ah-KEE, por fah-BOR.

c2.say: Trae nueve y son siete máximo. ¿Saca dos kilos o la documenta y paga?
c2.en: It's 9 and the maximum is 7. Will you take out two kilos, or check it and pay?

opts.why: Nueve is what the scale says. She is asking what you will do about it.
This was an either/or choice, so sí doesn't tell her which.

c2.ph: TRAH-eh NWEH-beh ee son SYEH-teh MAH-ksee-moh. SAH-kah dohs KEE-lohs oh lah doh-koo-MEN-tah ee PAH-gah?

end2.say: Muy bien, hágase a un ladito y cuando acabe me avisa.
end2.en: All right, step to the side and let me know when you're done.
end2.debrief: Some airlines weigh carry-ons too. The limits in this scene are made up, so check your own booking before you pack.
end2.ph: mwee byen, AH-gah-seh ah oon lah-DEE-toh ee KWAN-doh ah-KAH-beh meh ah-BEE-sah.

scenes.title: Pointing at the pots
scenes.blurb: Point, say uno de este, and find out what you are pointing at.

a.say: Pásele, ¿qué va a llevar? Hay tinga, chicharrón en salsa verde, rajas, picadillo.
a.en: Come on in, what will you have? There's tinga, chicharrón in green sauce, rajas, picadillo.
a.task: Point at a pot and ask for one.

opts.why: Hay is her listing what she has. She wants you to pick.
¿Qué va a llevar? just means what will you have here. She isn't asking about takeout.

a.ph: PAH-seh-leh, keh bah ah yeh-BAR? eye TEEN-gah, chee-chah-RRON en SAL-sah BEHR-deh, RAH-hahs, pee-kah-DEE-yoh.

b.say: ¿Ese? Es tinga de pollo. ¿Se lo sirvo en taco o en plato?
b.en: That one? It's chicken tinga. Shall I serve it in a taco or on a plate?

opts.why: This was an either/or question about how to serve it, and the tinga is already settled.

b.ph: EH-seh? ehs TEEN-gah deh POH-yoh. seh loh SEER-boh en TAH-koh oh en PLAH-toh?

c1.en: Would you like a double tortilla?

opts.en: Whether you want two tacos instead
opts.why: Doble tortilla is two tortillas stacked under one serving, not two servings.
Doble is about how many tortillas. She didn't say anything about the kind.

c2.say: Ahorita salen las tortillas, espéreme tantito.
c2.en: The tortillas are just coming out, hang on a moment.

opts.en: Order something else, they've run out
opts.why: Ahorita salen means they are coming out now. Nothing has run out.

opts.en: Wait a moment for the tortillas
Leave and come back much later
opts.why: Tantito means a little bit, so it's a very short wait.

c2.ph: ah-oh-REE-tah SAH-len lahs tor-TEE-yahs, ehs-PEH-reh-meh tan-TEE-toh.

d.en: Another one, or just that one?
d.task: Point at another pot and ask what it is.

opts.why: She asked whether you want another. At these counters you settle up at the end.
Ese is the one you already ordered, so this rejects your own food.

e.say: Son rajas con crema. Casi no pican.
e.en: Those are poblano strips with cream. They're barely spicy.

opts.why: She just told you: casi no pican means they are barely spicy.
Rajas are strips of poblano chile, so there is no meat in them.

e.ph: son RAH-hahs kon KREH-mah. KAH-see noh PEE-kan.

f.say: Órale. Cuando acabe me dice cuántos fueron y me paga.
f.en: OK. When you finish, tell me how many you had and pay me.

opts.why: Cuando acabe means when you finish, so you pay after.
Cuántos fueron is about counting what you ate. Everybody pays at the end.

f.ph: OH-rah-leh. KWAN-doh ah-KAH-beh meh DEE-seh KWAN-tohs FWEH-ron ee meh PAH-gah.

end.en: Here you go. Enjoy.
end.debrief: At a guisado counter you point, eat, and report how many you had when you pay. If you don't recognize a pot, ¿Qué es esto? is all you need.

scenes.title: Tasajo by weight
scenes.blurb: Buy meat by the half kilo in the Pasillo de Humo.

a.say: Pásele, pásele. ¿Qué le damos? Tasajo, cecina, chorizo.
a.en: Come in, come in. What can we get you? Tasajo, cecina, chorizo.
a.task: You want tasajo.

opts.why: He listed three kinds of meat, so uno doesn't tell him which.
Pásele is what vendors call out to invite you in. It isn't something to say back.

a.ph: PAH-seh-leh, PAH-seh-leh. keh leh DAH-mohs? tah-SAH-hoh, seh-SEE-nah, choh-REE-soh.

b.en: How much shall I give you? Half?

opts.why: Tasajo goes by weight, so he needs an amount, not a count. Medio means half a kilo.
Cuánto le doy asks how much meat you want. The price comes after he weighs it.

c1.say: Está a doscientos ochenta el kilo, entonces son ciento cuarenta.
c1.task: How much do you pay for your half kilo?

opts.why: Doscientos ochenta is the price of a whole kilo. You are buying half.
Ciento cuarenta is 140. Two hundred forty would be doscientos cuarenta.

c1.ph: ehs-TAH ah dohs-SYEN-tohs oh-CHEN-tah el KEE-loh, en-TON-sehs son SYEN-toh kwah-REN-tah.

c2.say: Uy, ya nada más me queda este pedazo, como cuatrocientos gramos. ¿Se lo doy?
c2.en: Oof, I only have this piece left, about 400 grams. Shall I give it to you?

opts.why: Nada más me queda este pedazo means this piece is all he has left.
Gramos is the weight of the piece. He hasn't given a price yet.

c2.ph: wee, yah NAH-dah mahs meh KEH-dah EHS-teh peh-DAH-soh, KOH-moh kwah-troh-SYEN-tohs GRAH-mohs. seh loh doy?

d.say: ¿Se lo aso aquí o se lo lleva crudo?
d.en: Shall I grill it here, or are you taking it raw?

opts.why: This was an either/or question, so sí doesn't tell him which.
Crudo means raw, and se lo aso aquí is the grilled option.

d.ph: seh loh AH-soh ah-KEE oh seh loh YEH-bah KROO-doh?

e.say: Órale. Siéntese ahí y ahorita se lo llevan.
e.en: OK. Sit down there and they'll bring it to you shortly.

opts.en: Take it to another stall to be cooked
opts.why: Siéntese ahí means sit down there, and he already offered to grill it.

opts.en: Stand here and carry it yourself
opts.why: Se lo llevan means they will bring it to you.

opts.en: Sit down and wait, they'll bring it

e.ph: OH-rah-leh. SYEN-teh-seh ah-EE ee ah-oh-REE-tah seh loh YEH-ban.

end.en: Enjoy, OK?
end.debrief: In the Pasillo de Humo you buy raw meat by weight and it is grilled for you. Prices are per kilo, and medio means half a kilo.

scenes.title: Tasting and buying mezcal
scenes.blurb: Taste joven or reposado, buy a bottle, get it wrapped.

a.say: Pásele. ¿Quiere probar? Tengo joven y reposado.
a.en: Come in. Would you like to taste? I have joven and reposado.
a.task: Say yes, and ask for the joven.

opts.why: Joven here is a style of mezcal, unaged. She isn't asking about you.
Reposado is mezcal rested in wood. Nobody is asking whether you want a rest.

a.ph: PAH-seh-leh. KYEH-reh proh-BAR? TEN-goh HOH-ben ee reh-poh-SAH-doh.

b.say: Este es espadín joven. Se toma a besitos, no de un jalón.
b.en: This is a young espadín. You drink it in little kisses, not in one go.

opts.why: A besitos describes tiny sips. Nobody expects you to kiss anything.
De un jalón means in one go, and she said not to.

b.ph: EHS-teh ehs ehs-pah-DEEN HOH-ben. seh TOH-mah ah beh-SEE-tohs, noh deh oon hah-LON.

c1.say: Salud. ¿Cómo lo siente? ¿Se lleva una botella?
c1.en: Cheers. How does it feel? Are you taking a bottle?
c1.task: You like it. Ask what a bottle costs.

opts.en: Yes. How much is the bottle?

opts.why: ¿Cómo lo siente? is about how the mezcal tastes to you, not how you feel.
Se lleva una botella is about buying a bottle to take with you.

c1.ph: sah-LOOD. KOH-moh loh SYEN-teh? seh YEH-bah OO-nah boh-TEH-yah?

c2.say: ¿Le doy a probar el reposado también?
c2.en: Shall I give you the reposado to taste too?
c2.task: Yes, you'd like to try it.

opts.why: You have just tried the joven. She is offering you the other one as well.
She is offering another taste, and you haven't bought anything yet.

c2.ph: leh doy ah proh-BAR el reh-poh-SAH-doh tam-BYEN?

c3.say: Este estuvo tres meses en barrica. ¿Cuál le gustó más?
c3.en: This one spent three months in the barrel. Which did you like more?
c3.task: You preferred the joven. Ask what a bottle costs.

opts.en: Yes, I liked it a lot, thanks.
opts.why: Cuál means which, so you need to name one.

opts.en: The joven. How much is it?

opts.why: Tres meses is how long it aged. Cuál asks which one you liked.

c3.ph: EHS-teh ehs-TOO-boh trehs MEH-sehs en bah-RREE-kah. kwal leh goos-TOH mahs?

d.say: La de setecientos cincuenta está en ochocientos cincuenta.

opts.why: Ochocientos is 800. Nine hundred would be novecientos.
Setecientos cincuenta is the bottle size in milliliters. The price is the second number.

d.ph: lah deh seh-teh-SYEN-tohs seen-KWEN-tah ehs-TAH en oh-choh-SYEN-tohs seen-KWEN-tah.

e.say: ¿Se la envuelvo? Para que no se rompa en la maleta.
e.en: Shall I wrap it? So it doesn't break in your suitcase.

opts.why: She isn't telling you how to pack. Envuelvo means she is offering to wrap it.
Para aquí would mean drinking it here. She is getting the bottle ready to travel.

e.ph: seh lah en-BWEL-boh? PAH-rah keh noh seh ROM-pah en lah mah-LEH-tah.

end.say: Listo. Aquí la tiene, bien envuelta. Salud.
end.en: All set. Here it is, well wrapped. Cheers.
end.debrief: Joven is unaged, and reposado rests in wood for a few months. Sip a besitos, and put bottles in checked luggage, not your carry-on.
end.ph: LEES-toh. ah-KEE lah TYEH-neh, byen en-BWEL-tah. sah-LOOD.
